insights.content: Warren Buffett's margin of safety concept - how far down is valuation vs assets. Want hard assets that provide protection against seizure or country risk.
2026 is a US midterm election year - historically not super bullish until after the election (September/November), then very strong afterward.

Greenland is strategically critical - controls North Atlantic, needed for nuclear submarines, centuries' most important trade route as Arctic ice melts. Whoever controls Greenland controls shipping between Asia and West (40% shorter than current routes).

insights.content: Taiwan invasion risk is real - Polymarket shows 13% chance in 2026. If China takes Taiwan, major chipmakers (Nvidia has 80% production there) would be severely impacted. Chinese stocks trading at discount may reflect this risk.
Year-end case trades (arsskiftescase) - stocks beaten down for tax-loss selling often recover strongly in January as flows return. Good timing strategy.
ETF flows driving individual stock moves - ARK Space and Defense ETF up 20% in a month, forcing purchases of Saab and other defense stocks regardless of individual valuation.

US electricity demand will surge with AI data centers. Tech companies buying nuclear reactors and mini-reactors. Trump said consumers shouldn't pay for build-out, tech companies must find own power solutions.
When geopolitics improves (Iran falls, Venezuela fell, Assad gone), it's bullish for Western markets - peace dividend like when Soviet fell. Russia and China lose influence spheres.

analysis_summary: Swedish trading podcast discussing year-start market moves, geopolitics, and investment cases for 2026. Key themes: defense sector rally (Saab up massively), hard assets rotation (uranium, silver, gold), space/satellite plays, and value investing. Hosts discuss Greenland/Taiwan geopolitical risks, year-end trading strategies, and present their annual stock picks including uranium ETFs, Snapchat, Kambi, GEO Group, and Bone Support. Strong bias toward commodities and away from pure AI plays.
